assumptions_and_scope: The threshold theorem assumes one single-parameter job, a fixed bidder set, an own-report-independent threshold, quasilinear utility, and objective allocation.
The threshold theorem proves unilateral weak dominance only; it does not prove coalition, false-name, repeated-game, capacity, effort, or delivery incentive compatibility.

The same-occurrence scarcity theorem assumes the late-bid cap is no greater than the original posted price; direct-option selection and multi-provider assignment remain Python and lifecycle obligations.
The capacity theorem proves aggregate attributed owner-weight preservation; it does not prove fixed-seed assignment invariance, uniform randomness, capacity authenticity, or ownership authenticity.

The cartel theorem assumes risk-neutral symmetric provers, perfect monitoring, stationary equal sharing or enforceable transfers, immediate grim-trigger punishment, and permanent zero punishment profit.
The bond theorem proves disposition conservation through an explicit structure; separate admission logic must prove that the bond covers named restitution.
The compilation grants no market, verifier, payment, settlement, token, release, or production authority.
